newsitem.title: USA: Duke Energy unit gets OK to expand pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Duke Energy unit gets OK to expand pipeline.

text.p: Duke Energy Corp unit Trunkline Gas Co said Wednesday the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved its $52 million expansion project July 22.

Trunkline said it will expand its Terrebonne natural gas pipeline system in offshore Louisiana by building and later operating a new platform and compressor station next to its existing T-25 platform in Ship Shoal Block 139.

The company said the new three-unit 28,950-horsepower station will increase capacity deliverable to its Centerville/Patterson, La., header station. It added the project is on schedule to close in the first quarter of 1998.

"This expansion will give Trunkline additional, efficient and cost-effective pipeline capacity for moving natural gas from significant newly developed offshore production areas to multiple onshore markets, said chairman Steve Roverud in a statement.
Rover added the new facilities will add capacity of 500 million cubic feet per day from the T-25 platform to multiple market outlets upstream of Trunkline's Patterson compressor station.

He also said several producers have committed significant new production to Trunkline's Terrebonne expansion, including Basin Exploration Inc of Delaware, Murphy Exploration & Production, Ocean Energy Inc, Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Offshore, Stone Energy Corp and Zilkha Energy.
